At Paysend , we're building the future of global payments - making money movement simple, fast, and accessible for everyone. As an Application Support Analyst, you'll play a critical role in delivering on that promise by ensuring our platforms run reliably and our customers can send and receive money without interruption.
The Application Support Analyst owns the health of our transaction ecosystem end to end: investigating individual transactions and broader flow anomalies, detecting issues before they escalate,supporting release deployments and post-release system verification, and driving incidents to resolution across both our B2C and Enterprise product lines. You'll work with large volumes of real-time payment data, using tools like Oracle SQL, Postman, OpenSearch, and Grafana to trace transactions, diagnose root causes, and keep critical payment services running smoothly.
This role is ideal for someone who enjoys solving complex problems, thrives in a fast-paced environment, and wants to make a tangible impact on the experience of millions of customers around the world.

• Transaction Administration: Analyze, track, and manage end-to-end payment transaction flows using Oracle SQL, Postman, and OpenSearch.

• Incident Management & Resolution: Conduct incident response efforts, including root-cause investigations, documentation of incident reports, and coordination of cross-functional teams to resolution.

• Stuck & Flagged Transaction Handling: Resolve transactions flagged for manual parsing and investigate payouts or funding stuck in pending status (>3 days), updating statuses or escalating as needed.

• SAR & PDP Reconciliation: Troubleshoot SAR reconciliation issues, including unmatched transactions, missing/duplicate report data, and platform data mismatches.

• Releases & Deployment: Coordinate, execute, and roll back service releases, verifying post-release system health and performance graphs.

• Problem-solving mindset with the drive to investigate novel issues and determine solution steps independently

• Monitoring & Operations: Basic Linux, network, or cloud administration experience.

• Incident & Escalation Management: Ability to manage concurrent, time-sensitive incidents under strict SLA windows, moving from root-cause analysis to final resolution.

• Cross-Functional Collaboration: Experience interfacing with external entities (banks, PSPs, processors) and internal stakeholders (Engineering, Settlement, Customer Support).

• Programming Literacy: Basic skills in any programming language to read code, run scripts, or inspect data payloads.

• Communication Skills: Advanced written and verbal English skills for managing communications with internal teams and external financial partners.

Nice To Have

• Experience working directly with OpenSearch for log and transaction analysis.

• Hands-on experience with team collaboration tools (Slack, Google Workspace, Jira, Confluence).

description:
ABOUT BASETEN

Baseten powers mission-critical inference for the world's most dynamic AI companies, like Cursor, Notion, OpenEvidence, Abridge, Clay, Gamma, and Writer. By uniting applied AI research, flexible infrastructure, and seamless developer tooling, we enable companies operating at the frontier of AI to bring cutting-edge models into production. We're growing quickly and recently raised our $1.5B Series F https://www.baseten.co/blog/announcing-our-series-f/, led by Altimeter Capital, Conviction Partners, and Spark Capital. Join us and help build the platform engineers turn to ship AI products.

THE ROLE

Every agent on Baseten Sandboxes gets its own microVM, where it writes and runs code, calls tools, and keeps state across long tasks. Agents pause and resume constantly, so the machine underneath has to start, stop, snapshot, fork, and resume fast, and keep every tenant isolated while it does. General-purpose virtualization was not built for that workload.

The Agent Infra team builds that layer. Sandboxes run in microVMs with custom Linux kernels on bare-metal servers we operate. You'll own how sandboxes start, stop, snapshot, fork, and resume, and how they perform on each host's CPU and memory, down to the hardware. You'll also own the guest and host side of each sandbox: its identity, how it attaches to different storage classes for performance or capabilities, and the virtual devices that connect it securely to the network. In September 2026, Baseten acquired Blaxel https://www.baseten.co/blog/blaxel-is-joining-baseten-to-build-the-future-of-agentic-cloud/, whose microVM sandboxes are the foundation for Baseten Sandboxes https://docs.baseten.co/sandboxes.

We are building a cloud, not just using one. That means designing for many tenants from day one and thinking through what each decision means all the way down to the datacenter. The team is small and ownership is big: we ship in weeks and months, not multi-year programs.

If you've worked deep in KVM and Firecracker, Cloud Hypervisor, or QEMU and want to build the computers AI agents run on, we'd love to talk.

EXAMPLE INITIATIVES

- Baseten Sandboxes documentation https://docs.baseten.co/sandboxes

- Own the microVM lifecycle for agent sandboxes: start, stop, suspend, resume, snapshot, and fork

- Build and tune the custom guest kernels sandboxes run on

- Tune host CPU and memory configuration so sandboxes run fast and safely on each type of hardware we operate

- Manage host-level resources and sandbox density on each machine

- Own startup and resume performance end to end, from VM boot or snapshot restore to the first command

- Own the guest and host side of each sandbox: its identity, how it attaches to storage, and the virtual devices that connect it to the network

- Design isolation for multi-tenant workloads where the hypervisor is the security boundary

- Debug virtualization and isolation issues at scale, from userspace through the kernel to the hardware

- Contribute architecture decisions and code back to the open-source projects we build on

REQUIREMENTS

- Hands-on experience with KVM, plus Firecracker, Cloud Hypervisor, or QEMU

- Deep understanding of Linux internals: namespaces, cgroups, memory management, and the boot path

- Experience building cloud infrastructure as the provider (multi-tenant compute that customers run on), not only running workloads on a cloud provider

- Experience building multi-tenant infrastructure where isolation is a security boundary

- Strong systems programming background in Rust and/or Go; C/C++ also welcome

- Experience debugging performance and correctness problems across userspace and kernel boundaries
